1. More conv capacity always helps. If false, adding a conv gains little when a conv already sits on a parallel or serial path.
2. avg_pool_3x3 and skip_connect are interchangeable parameter-free fillers. If false, a conv edit gains differently depending on which one is the neighbor.
3. Stacking 3x3 convs in series raises the receptive field and so helps. If false, a 3x3 upstream makes a further 3x3 downstream redundant.
4. A direct 0->3 shortcut is helpful and independent of the rest of the cell. If false, it makes extra deep-path capacity on edge 4 less valuable.
5. Edits are roughly additive across edges. If false, an edit on a node's output edges does nothing when the node's input is cut.
6. Upgrading 1x1 to 3x3 is a uniform gain. If false, the gain shrinks when the replaced op is already a conv.
7. Removing the shortcut edge is uniformly harmful. If false, it costs much less when a strong deep conv path exists.
8. Interaction signs transfer across datasets. If false, ImageNet16-120 would flip the sign relative to CIFAR-10. I only propose hypotheses where I expect a consistent sign.
